1. The theorem and encoded boundary

Fix the algebraic universal alphabet
$\mathcal G=
\{X,H,S,\mathrm{CNOT},CZ,\mathrm{Toffoli},
\mathrm{SWAP},\mathrm{reset},\mathrm{discard},I\}.$
Let $S$ bound the circuit’s gate count and wire count; otherwise replace $S$ below by $S+n$. For every rational $\epsilon>0$, the construction produces a two-dimensional implementation $\mathcal P_C$ and data maps
$\mathcal E_{n,r},\qquad \mathcal D_{n,r},$
such that, for every stipulated local-stochastic fault process below the threshold,
$\boxed{
\left\|
\mathcal D_{n,r}\circ\mathcal P_C\circ\mathcal E_{n,r}
-\mathcal U_C
\right\|_\diamond\le \epsilon .
}$
The diamond norm here is not divided by two. The statement includes arbitrary untouched references.

The encoding and decoding maps depend on width and concatenation level, not on the circuit’s gate choices. The level is selected from a uniform size bound, rather than from a gate-dependent optimized compilation.

The unknown-input promise is explicit: the input arrives through $\mathcal E_{n,r}$, already encoded on the designated native carriers. A physical loading interface must deliver that boundary or a separately warranted correctable boundary-noise contract. This does not provide a reliable encoder for an arbitrary bare, unprotected unknown qubit. Known states and all work states are physically prepared through the noisy native menu.

There is also an actual destructive-readout channel $\mathcal M_{n,r}$, including local classical processing, with
$\boxed{
\left\|
\mathcal M_{n,r}\circ\mathcal P_C\circ\mathcal E_{n,r}
-\mathcal Z^{\otimes n}\circ\mathcal U_C
\right\|_\diamond\le\epsilon .
}$
An ideal final quantum recovery is not executed to obtain this classical output.

The supplied papers retain their stated scopes. The non-Abelian construction uses global classical decoding and an ideal comparison recovery; it explicitly distinguishes that memory result from complete preparation and readout. The local Pauli architecture requires additional independence for its universal extension. Those missing operations are supplied separately here. arxiv.org+1 <https://arxiv.org/html/2611.08488v1?utm_source=chatgpt.com>
